boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named RISD spaces for research, making, critique, exhibitions, and campus resources.

cards.title: Fleet Library at RISD
cards.subtitle: Roger Mandle Building, Providence
cards.notes: Use the main reading room to pull art and design references, then ask library staff for help locating specialized physical or digital materials.
cards.short_summary: A historic banking hall repurposed for art and design research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says Fleet Library has more than 150,000 circulating books and resources in art, design, architecture, and related fields.
cards.access_notes: RISD identifies the library as a campus resource; confirm current visitor and borrowing access with Fleet Library.

cards.title: RISD Museum
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Bring a sketchbook for a close-looking session, or check the museum calendar for lectures, concerts, and screenings before you go.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum collection connecting visual research with public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD states that students have access to lectures, concerts, screenings, and more than 90,000 works at the RISD Museum.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: RISD lists it as a campus resource; consult the museum directly for current entry and program details.

cards.title: Co-Works Research Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Check current peer-tutoring or sponsored-studio opportunities when a project needs advanced tools or cross-departmental feedback.
cards.short_summary: A research lab organized around advanced tools and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD describes Co-Works as a cross-departmental research space with peer tutoring, sponsored studios, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Use is tied to RISD programming and resources; verify current lab access and support offerings before visiting.

cards.title: Color Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Use the materials and object collection to compare color relationships in person, then translate observations into your studio tests.
cards.short_summary: A materials-focused setting for investigating color across disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Color Lab’s collection of materials and objects supports exploration of color across art and design fields.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: RISD lists the lab as a campus resource; confirm current access procedures with the relevant department.

cards.title: Movement Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Look for current experimental research or active-learning sessions if your work involves movement, performance, or embodied design.
cards.short_summary: A setting for research and exchange through movement.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Movement Lab supports investigation of movement’s social, cultural, ecological, and expressive properties.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Programming and access may vary; check with RISD before planning a visit.

cards.title: Edna W. Lawrence Nature Lab
cards.subtitle: Waterman Building, 13 Waterman Street
cards.notes: Study specimens or imaging resources for a project connecting art, design, and science; arrange any requested room or equipment use in advance.
cards.short_summary: A natural-history collection and imaging resource for hands-on visual research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Nature Lab provides advanced imaging systems and access to more than 80,000 specimens for design research.
cards.source_title: RISD Nature Lab Collections and Research Lab | RISD
cards.access_notes: The Nature Lab describes reservation forms for some rooms and equipment; contact the lab to confirm current availability.

cards.entity_name: Studio for Research in Sound and Technology
cards.title: Studio for Research in Sound and Technology
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Explore current studio or independent-research options when a project calls for sound composition, soundscape work, or acoustic simulation.
cards.short_summary: A hub for experimental sound work and research.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says this studio supports sonic experimentation, experimental music composition, soundscape design, and acoustic simulation.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Studios and independent research are program-dependent; verify current access with RISD.

cards.title: Sustainability Design Lab
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Use the lab’s low-impact design focus to frame material or site questions, and check for current projects open to student participation.
cards.short_summary: A lab linking interior and landscape architecture through sustainability.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says the Sustainability Design Lab develops low-impact design strategies and inclusive material cultures at the intersection of interior and landscape architecture.
cards.source_title: Academic Resources and Galleries on Campus | RISD
cards.access_notes: Confirm current lab programming and participation options with RISD.

cards.title: Gelman Student Exhibitions Gallery
cards.subtitle: Entrance to the RISD Museum, Providence
cards.notes: See a current student-curated group exhibition, then review proposal details if you want to develop a show with other students.
cards.short_summary: A gallery for student-proposed and student-curated group exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD says students may propose and curate group shows at the Gelman Student Exhibitions Gallery, located at the RISD Museum entrance.
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions change; check RISD’s current exhibition information before visiting or proposing a show.

cards.title: Woods-Gerry Gallery
cards.subtitle: RISD campus, Providence
cards.notes: Visit an undergraduate exhibition to see how work is prepared and mounted, and watch for opportunities to participate in campus shows.
cards.short_summary: RISD’s primary venue for undergraduate exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD identifies Woods-Gerry Gallery as its primary venue for undergraduate work and says students gain experience preparing, mounting, and publicly sharing work there.
cards.access_notes: Gallery schedules change throughout the academic year; verify the current exhibition before visiting.
